comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers evaluated the same claims (C2, C3, C50, C58, C60, C63, C64, C91) as SUPPORTED, confirming that T cells respond equivalently to ancestral and variant spike proteins with strong converging evidence from multiple analytical approaches.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations address identical claims (C4, C5, C49, C65-C69) as SUPPORTED, accepting the dose-dependent phenotypic changes in infection-naïve individuals with consistent evidence from quantitative and phenotypic analyses.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations address the same claims (C9, C37, C99) as SUPPORTED, accepting the conclusion that single-dose vaccination may be sufficient for convalescents, though both acknowledge this is based on immunological surrogates rather than clinical efficacy data.

Agreement with different scope. OpenEval evaluated C6, C53, C55, C75, C76 as SUPPORTED with caveats about small sample size. Peer reviewers evaluated C6, C75, C76 as SUPPORTED without challenging the findings, though they raised concerns about sample size elsewhere (R10). Both accept the longitudinal findings in convalescents.

Strong agreement on uncertainty. Both evaluations address overlapping claims (C7, C8, C80-C87) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes conclusions are inferential based on marker expression rather than functional assays. Peer reviewers similarly questioned the functional significance, noting the study is 'very descriptive' and asking 'which of these T cell subsets studied are protective and how.'

Perfect agreement on speculation. Both evaluations address C110 and C111 as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval explicitly notes these are hypotheses requiring direct testing. Peer reviewers questioned 'what it all means' and requested acknowledgement of how future studies could validate protective roles. Both recognize the need for longitudinal follow-up.

Disagreement. OpenEval evaluated methodological claims (C45-C48, C51-C52) as SUPPORTED, viewing IFNγ-based identification as validated. Peer reviewers expressed UNCERTAINTY about C45-C48, specifically questioning whether IFNγ-based identification captured all relevant T cell populations, noting cTfh cells are poor IFNγ producers.

Disagreement on implications. OpenEval evaluated study design claims (C38-C44) as SUPPORTED but noted small sample size as a limitation. Peer reviewers expressed UNCERTAINTY, with Reviewer #2 stating 'the groups are small 5 vs 6' and requesting expanded group sizes and serological data to strengthen confidence in the cohort characterization.

OpenEval evaluated CD8+ T cell phenotypic differences (C92-C95) as SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical analyses. No corresponding peer review evaluation was found specifically addressing these claims, though they may have been implicitly accepted as part of broader phenotypic findings.

OpenEval evaluated literature-based claims about epitope conservation (C22-C27) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide important context validated by current study data. No corresponding peer review evaluation was found specifically addressing these background claims.

Peer reviewers evaluated claims about outlier handling and unexpected findings (C55-C57) as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the statistical approach without dispute. OpenEval addressed C55 within R3 but did not create a separate evaluation for C56-C57.

Peer reviewers expressed UNCERTAINTY about high CCR6 expression (C62), questioning whether it was surprising given IFNγ-producing cells are typically Th1/CXCR3-associated. No corresponding OpenEval evaluation was found specifically addressing this phenotypic interpretation concern.
